target_customer: Spanish speaking individuals in Latin America paying directly for online therapy, and employers buying mental wellbeing benefits
problem: Demand for mental health care among Spanish speakers in Latin America outstrips access to credentialed psychologists and psychiatrists.
business_model: Marketplace connecting users to independent specialists with per session fees (B2C) plus B2B employee wellbeing contracts
product_category: Online therapy marketplace, digital mental health

founders.name: Santiago de Bedout
founders.background_notes: YC page: early Rappi employee (2016) who led the liquor delivery unit; built tech products and managed engineering, sales, growth and operations teams. Valora Analitik (2024) calls him CEO and co-founder; no other cofounders named in sources.

competitors.name: Terapify
competitors.what: Mexico based online therapy platform for individuals and employers

competitors.name: BetterHelp
competitors.what: Large international online therapy service with resources for Hispanic and Latino users

competitors.name: Enterapia
competitors.what: Bogota based online psychotherapy by video and chat

technical_complexity.rationale: Video sessions, scheduling, matching and payments are standard; the hard part is supply of credentialed providers and local compliance.

defensibility.rationale: Provider network and Spanish language focus help, but competitors can recruit the same psychologists and the marketplace has low switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquisition found. Local rivals such as Terapify and Enterapia remained independent in the sources found.

market_need_then: Pandemic era rise in demand for mental health services in Latin America and a shortage of providers; the company cites B2B clients such as Experian, Starbucks and Habi.

identity.voice_and_tone: Warm consumer wellbeing tone in Spanish, with a blog, podcast and free psychological tests

branding.brand_signature: Won the 2023 Forbes 30 Under 30 Latinx Pitch Competition, with the winner announced on stage by Bad Bunny
branding.community_and_virality: Press mentions in Colombian media (Portafolio, El Tiempo, RCN) and the Forbes pitch win; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Recognized in Colombian press and boosted by the Forbes pitch win, but no evidence of a distinctive identity asset.

outcome_analysis: Selia joined YC in Winter 2022 and kept operating as a Spanish language therapy marketplace. Company figures claim more than 400 thousand sessions and 700 specialists, and Valora Analitik reported 2024 revenue expectations above 4 million dollars. Funding visible in public sources is small, so growth appears to be driven largely by revenue; the long term outcome is not yet known.
notes: Aggregator funding figures conflict and are unverified: Seedtable 1.5M seed in 2022-03, CB Insights 700K over 4 rounds, VCBacked 500K, a 200K round in 2023-10, and YC 500K mentioned by one source. The 300K Forbes prize is reported by Hola and Portafolio. Competitor sources are CB Insights comparison pages, which are undated, so traction and funding then are unknown. Valora Analitik 2024-07-27 says revenue above 4M expected by year end (company claim). Founding year 2021 on YC, 2020 on some profiles.
